{

  "headline": "Intake established the browser game’s scope, delivery assumptions, and discovery questions.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "answers": [
    {"id": "K1.1", "basis": "S1", "answer": "One person plays against the computer through a browser page."},
    {"id": "K1.2", "basis": "S1", "answer": "The player can complete a game against the computer, see shot results and the game outcome, and start another game."},
    {"id": "K2.1", "basis": "S1", "answer": "Build a small single-player browser Battleship game against the computer. Multiplayer, accounts, persistence, and deployment are outside the assumed scope."},
    {"id": "K2.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "The repository is stated to be empty, so there is no existing application behavior to preserve; discovery should verify the checkout before implementation."},
    {"id": "K3.1", "basis": "inspect", "answer": "Discovery must establish the available environment and define the page interactions, game messages, files, and any server endpoints; exact names and shapes are not supplied by the request."},
    {"id": "K3.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Discovery must define meaningful HTTP statuses and errors for the chosen interface; no particular codes or error messages are specified."},
    {"id": "K4.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Use conventional Battleship rules, a small fixed board and fleet, alternating turns, and victory when one fleet is sunk; discovery must record the exact dimensions, fleet, placement rules, and turn behavior."},
    {"id": "K4.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Reject or prevent malformed, out-of-bounds, repeated, or otherwise illegal actions according to the recorded game rules; discovery must define the exact action shapes and placement constraints."},
    {"id": "K5.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "A game has ephemeral state owned by its single browser session, including both boards, shots, turn, and outcome; it lasts until a new game, session end, or restart, with no cross-session persistence assumed. Discovery must choose its runtime location."},
    {"id": "K5.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "The player sees their board and shot results, while unhit computer ship positions remain hidden during play. No sharing or concurrent multi-person changes are supported; a restart may discard the game."},
    {"id": "K6.1", "basis": "inspect", "answer": "Use Node.js for the server; discovery must establish the available Node.js version and record a compatible supported version for the project."},
    {"id": "K6.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Prefer Node.js built-ins and avoid unnecessary dependencies; discovery may select a dependency if needed and must record it."},
    {"id": "K6.3", "basis": "inspect", "answer": "Discovery must determine the available runtime and define the startup command, port configuration, and project files; assume no external services or secrets."},
    {"id": "K7.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Keep game rules and computer decisions testable independently of browser rendering and server transport; discovery must choose the actual module boundaries."},
    {"id": "K8.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Use Node.js’s built-in test runner if supported by the selected runtime, with a documented test command; discovery must verify compatibility."},
    {"id": "K8.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Check rules, invalid actions, computer turns, and win conditions in automated tests; also verify the served browser entry point and a complete playable flow at their real boundaries. Discovery must choose the browser-check method."},
    {"id": "K9.1", "basis": "S1", "answer": "The result must be usable in a browser served by Node.js. Assume local delivery with a documented startup command; no named deployed target or external access is supplied."},
    {"id": "K10.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Keep the game responsive and understandable, with usable controls and visible game status; use basic accessible semantics and prevent illegal moves. No numeric performance or security targets are specified."},
    {"id": "K11.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "The main rejection risks are an unplayable browser flow, incorrect rules or computer turns, exposed hidden ships, and tests that miss the actual served experience."},
    {"id": "K11.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Early evidence would be a served-page smoke check, tests of representative legal and illegal turns and game endings, and an inspection of what the browser can see during play."}

  "summary": "S1 [fact]: Deliver a small browser-playable, single-player Battleship game against the computer; the named browser is the authorized usability target. [Assumption]: Local use is sufficient because no deployed target is named; no accounts, multiplayer, shared state, or persistence are included. [Assumption]: The runtime identifies the player by a single browser session; each game is ephemeral, ends in victory, defeat, a new game, session end, or restart, and does not survive a restart. The player’s board and shot results are visible to the player; unhit computer ship positions stay hidden during play. [Open: discovery]: Establish what the browser and server runtime provide, then record the exact board, fleet, placement, turn, visibility, and end rules; this blocks the game contract and its checks. Establish the action and state interfaces before deciding where ephemeral state lives and how illegal or concurrent actions are handled; this blocks implementation and boundary tests. S2 [fact]: Use Node.js for the server and include tests. [Open: discovery]: Inspect the checkout and available runtime first, then establish the Node.js version, startup and test commands, configuration, files, dependencies, any endpoints, statuses and errors, and browser-check method; these block implementation and verification. [Fact]: The exercise states that the repository is empty and supplies no team, workspace, channel, internal site, private repository, owner, or prior-run source hint; Node.js documentation and the eventual checkout and environment are discovery leads, not verified findings. No sensitive locator is supplied; any discovered sensitive locator belongs only in an authorized private store, never committed KNOWLEDGE/. [Boundary]: This intake implements nothing and adds no deployment or other product scope. In an isolated run, the source checkout remains at its snapshot until the final return; the delivered outcome becomes visible there at final return and, if a deployment is later authorized, in that target only after release."
}
